# AGENTS.md — CI/CD

Guidance for the repo's CI/CD: the workflows in this directory. The rest of
the monorepo is documented in the root AGENTS.md.

## Workflows — `workflows/ci.yml`

Main pipeline: every push to `main` and every pull request. The four
app-testing jobs share one bootstrap: checkout, pnpm, Node 22, `pnpm
install --frozen-lockfile` (the committed lockfile is authoritative —
drift fails CI). The `docker` job differs by design: it installs nothing
— the image build does all installs — and starts from checkout + buildx.
CI never deploys: Railway builds its own image from
`apps/server/Dockerfile`, which the `docker` job exists to verify.

- `check` — build → lint → typecheck. Build-first is load-bearing:
  `routeTree.gen.ts` and `src/paraglide/**` are git-ignored files
  generated by Vite plugins, so typecheck cannot resolve them until a
  build ran once. Turbo's cache is persisted via `actions/cache` on
  `.turbo/` (turbo's default 2.x cache dir), keyed per-commit with a
  prefix restore — turbo hashes inputs itself, so a restored cache can
  never replay a stale result.
- `unit` — `test:unit` with NO database service, on purpose: unit suites
  must pass with nothing to connect to, keeping the unit/integration
  split honest.
- `integration` — Postgres service container, then `db:check` (catches a
  schema edit that never had `db:generate` run — as drift, not a
  confusing "column does not exist" later), then `db:test:setup` +
  `test:integration`.
- `e2e` — Playwright against the `ci` environment's S3 bucket; browsers
  cached by resolved Playwright version, not lockfile hash; upload specs
  skip themselves when S3 secrets are absent (fork PRs). Capped at 60
  minutes — the default 6-hour job timeout is no bound for a hung spec.
- `docker` — builds `apps/server/Dockerfile` (push: false — this job
  exists to fail the commit) and asserts:
  1. the VITE_* build args reached the built web bundle — the regression
     this job exists for, since a missing `ARG` silently ships a bundle
     with no OAuth buttons;
  2. the `__APP_VERSION__` define reached the bundle (same failure mode
     as the VITE_* ARGs — a broken define crashes the footer at runtime);
  3. the migration runner (`apps/server/dist/migrate.js`) and migration
     SQL (`packages/db/drizzle/`) shipped in the image;
  4. the runner installed only the server's production dependencies — no
     `apps/web/node_modules` may exist (issue #58's regression), while
     the server's own prod deps must be present.
- The `docker` job then RUNS what it built, because the E2E suite runs
  the dev server and the four assertions above only inspect files: the
  pre-deploy migration is executed against a Postgres service container,
  the image is booted with its real CMD (`node apps/server/dist/
index.js`, no overrides — the exact process Railway starts) on
  `--network host` (the runner is a native Linux VM, so host networking
  reaches the published service ports on localhost), and three probes
  must pass: `/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}` (DB-backed), `/login`
  serves the static SPA shell, and `/` 302s to `/login?redirect=...` (the
  page gate is live). The boot then closes the second half of the OAuth
  provider mirror (the bundle grep is the first): the container carries
  dummy OAuth credential pairs and `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT=false` (one IP drives
  the probes, same escape hatch as the E2E stack), and `/api/auth/
sign-in/social` must offer a redirect for exactly `google`, `discord`
  and `twitch` — with `github` as the control probe, which must be
  refused — so a provider the client offers but the server has no
  credentials for (or the reverse) fails here instead of silently
  breaking a button in production.

## Workflows — `workflows/smoke.yml`

Production smoke check — the standing replacement for a post-deploy
check, since CI never deploys. Probes the live `mytuums.com` (the
Railway production environment's custom domain) with the same three
checks as the docker job's boot step: health endpoint, `/login` serving
the SPA shell, and the page gate's redirect. Runs every 6 hours
(`schedule`) and on demand (`workflow_dispatch` — run it right after a
deploy). No checkout, no secrets, no repo writes.

## Secrets

- `check`, `unit`, `integration`, `docker`: none.
- `e2e`: the `S3_*` set (the `ci` bucket, never production).
- `smoke.yml`: none.

## Load-bearing decisions — do not break

- Every third-party GitHub Action is pinned to a full commit SHA — never a
  mutable tag, which can be silently repointed (see the trivy-action and
  kics-github-action compromises). The trailing `# vN` comment records the
  tag for the next bump: re-resolve the tag, update the SHA, keep the
  comment in step.
- CI never points at the production bucket: e2e cleanup deletes objects
  by prefix (`truncateAll()`), so a shared bucket would let CI and a
  local run delete each other's objects mid-test.
- The integration/e2e jobs write a `.env` file because every `db:*` and
  e2e script runs through `dotenv -e .env`, which errors on a missing
  file. dotenv does not override already-set variables, so workflow
  `env:` wins.
- The `docker` job's boot step uses `--network host` and `localhost`
  service URLs — that combination only works on a native Linux VM runner
  (ubuntu-latest). Moving to a container-based or macOS runner would
  silently break the smoke step; switch to `host.docker.internal` +
  service-account networking if the runner fleet ever changes.

## Commands

Nothing to build here.
